claims.text: TaVCrW is initially a disordered BCC solid solution at 0 K.
Short-range order stabilizes TaVCrW by approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
An MTP trained on GGA-PBE energies and forces can replace the EAM reference potential for TaVCrW.
A sequence of intermediate lambda states permits FEP to compute the solid-liquid free-energy difference in place of thermodynamic integration.
The relevant structural mediator is the MTP's reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distributions of both solid and liquid TaVCrW.
Capturing local atomic environments and SRO makes the surrogate reproduce the pertinent free-energy landscape.
Accurate phase-space overlap allows FEP to converge rapidly without slow path-dependent thermodynamic integration.
The MTP is a computationally efficient surrogate for the DFT potential-energy surface and can generate the large ensembles required by FEP.
The MTP can retain the approximately 2-3 meV/atom SRO contribution needed for accurate melting calculations.
Electronic gaps or related electronic-excitation effects shift the melting point and can be captured by the proposed MTP treatment.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The TaVCrW melting temperature predicted by MTP plus FEP will be within 10 K of the TOR-TILD result.
The FEP solid-liquid free-energy difference will agree with the TI result within 0.5 meV/atom.
A supercell containing at least 128 atoms is required to sample the SRO contribution adequately.
The 2000-2400 K range is sufficient to sample the liquid fully and capture the TaVCrW melting transition.
High-temperature magnetic fluctuations can be neglected or represented through a post-hoc electronic-entropy correction.
Finite-temperature magnetic fluctuations may materially affect calculated thermodynamic properties.
GGA-PBE underbinding or overbinding errors for V and Cr at 0 K may propagate into the liquid free energy.
FEP convergence for a complex SRO-bearing liquid is sensitive to the lambda schedule and MTP training-set quality.
A controlled benchmark against TOR-TILD will compare melting temperature, solid-liquid free energy, CPU time, and liquid SRO under identical cell-size and temperature conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism attribute electronic-excitation accuracy directly to the MTP, whereas the conditions and boundary treat related finite-temperature effects as omitted from training and handled through a post-hoc correction. It is therefore unclear whether these effects reside in the MTP or in a separate correction.

The predicted outcome independently requires cost reduction above 80% and melting-temperature agreement within 10 K, but the falsification rule only rejects the cost/temperature part when cost reduction is below 80% and the temperature error is above 10 K simultaneously. Failure of either individual prediction can therefore escape falsification.
